subQuestions.questionText: Which female scientist took X-rays of the DNA molecule and concluded that DNA is helix-shaped?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Franklin took X-ray diffraction images of DNA that revealed its helical structure.

subQuestions.questionText: A cell with 14 chromosomes undergoes meiosis. What is the number of chromatids in this cell at the beginning of meiosis?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
At the beginning of meiosis each chromosome has been replicated and consists of 2 chromatids, so 14 chromosomes × 2 = 28 chromatids.

subQuestions.questionText: In the inheritance of blood groups there are …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
ABO blood groups are determined by three alleles (I^A, I^B, i) and result in four phenotypes (A, B, AB, O).

options.A: two phenotypes controlled by three alleles.
options.B: three phenotypes controlled by two alleles.
options.C: four phenotypes controlled by three alleles.
options.D: four phenotypes controlled by two alleles.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statements relate to cell division:
(i) Crossing over occurs
(ii) Contributes to genetic variation in a population
(iii) Produces cells with a diploid number of chromosomes
(iv) Produces somatic cells only

Which ONE of the following combinations of statements refer to meiosis?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Only (i) crossing over and (ii) contribution to genetic variation are characteristic of meiosis. Statements (iii) and (iv) describe mitosis.

subQuestions.questionText: The opossums and wombats are believed to have originated from a common ancestor. The shaded parts of the diagram show the distribution of these species (opossums in South America, wombats in Australia). The type of evidence for evolution that is represented in the diagram is ... (Refer to the map diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The geographical distribution of related species across different continents is biogeographical evidence for evolution.

subQuestions.questionText: A plant with yellow (y) and round (R) peas is crossed with a plant with green (Y) and wrinkled (r) peas. Which ONE of the following are the possible genotypes of the parents (P₁)?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Yellow (y) is recessive and round (R) is dominant in this question. Yellow round = yyRR; green wrinkled = YYrr.

subQuestions.questionText:
A segment of DNA contains:
• 31% of adenine in strand 1
• 12% of cytosine in strand 2
• 27% of guanine in strand 2

In this segment of DNA, there will also be …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
DNA strands are complementary and antiparallel. Adenine in strand 1 pairs with thymine in strand 2, so 31% adenine in strand 1 means 31% thymine in strand 2.

subQuestions.questionText:
Two people each gave four descriptions about themselves:
P: Tongue rolling (can / cannot)
Q: Height (150 cm / 153 cm)
R: Earlobes (unattached / attached)
S: Blood group (A / AB)

Which ONE of the following combinations are examples of discontinuous variation?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Discontinuous variation has distinct categories with no intermediates: tongue rolling (P), earlobes (R) and blood group (S). Height (Q) is continuous variation.

subQuestions.questionText: The phase in meiosis where chromatids are pulled towards poles is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate and are pulled to opposite poles. In anaphase I, whole chromosomes (not chromatids) separate.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: A genetic disorder that results in a person who cannot distinguish between the colours red and green.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term: The structure that joins two chromatids together.
subQuestions.memoText: Centromere ✓ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.

Description: The type of dominance in which neither of the two alleles is dominant over each other, resulting in an offspring with an intermediate phenotype.
A: Complete dominance
B: Co-dominance
subQuestions.memoText:
None ✓✓ (2 marks)
This description fits incomplete dominance, not complete dominance (A) and not co-dominance (B). In co-dominance both alleles are fully expressed (not intermediate).

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.

Description: The point where two chromatids overlap during crossing over.
A: Chiasma
B: Locus
subQuestions.memoText:
A only ✓✓ (2 marks)
A chiasma is the point where chromatids cross over. A locus is the position of a gene on a chromosome.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none.

Description: The scientist who proposed the law of segregation.
A: Darwin
B: Lamarck
subQuestions.memoText:
None ✓✓ (2 marks)
The law of segregation was proposed by Mendel, not Darwin (A) or Lamarck (B).

subQuestions.questionText: (Refer to the karyotype diagram of a gamete in the question paper, showing an extra chromosome at position 23.) Name the type of mutation that occurred during the production of this gamete.

subQuestions.memoText:

XXY ✓✓ / XYX (2 marks)
The abnormal sperm carries XY; fusion with a normal egg (X) gives XXY.

(a) CCU ✓ (1 mark)
(b) GTA ✓✓ (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: During the synthesis of the same protein, there was a change in the amino acid sequence because alanine was replaced by tryptophan. Explain the possible reason for this.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 3 of:
- A mutation occurred ✓
- that changed the sequence of nitrogenous bases on DNA from GGG to GAA ✓ / when A replaced G
- mRNA codon changed from CCC to CUU ✓ / when U replaced C
- causing tRNA to bring a different amino acid ✓
(3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe transcription.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 6 of:
- The DNA double helix unwinds ✓
- The DNA strands unzip ✓ / weak hydrogen bonds break
- to form two separate strands ✓
- One strand is used as a template ✓
- to form mRNA ✓
- using free RNA nucleotides ✓ from the nucleoplasm
- The mRNA is complementary to the DNA ✓ / A pairs with U, G pairs with C and T pairs with A
- mRNA now has the coded message ✓ for protein synthesis
(6 marks)

subQuestions.memoText:
Produces spindle fibres ✓ (1 mark)
(Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the contribution of metaphase I to natural selection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 6 of:
- Random arrangement of chromosomes ✓ at the equator
- results in the formation of genetically different gametes ✓
- This leads to increased genetic variation in a population ✓
- which will cause some individuals to have favourable and some to have unfavourable characteristics ✓
- When environmental conditions change ✓
- those with favourable characteristics will survive ✓
- and those with unfavourable characteristics will die ✓
(6 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a bar graph to represent the percentage of land used to grow Bt corn from 1995 to 2010.
subQuestions.memoText:
Criteria for marking the graph:
- Bar graph is drawn (T): 1 mark
- Caption of the graph includes both variables (C): 1 mark (e.g. "Percentage land used to grow Bt corn from 1995 to 2010")
- Correct labels on the X-axis and Y-axis with correct unit on the Y-axis (L): 1 mark (X: Years; Y: Land used to grow Bt corn (%))
- Correct scale for Y-axis AND bars of equal width and equal spaces for X-axis (S): 1 mark
- Plotting (P) correctly done:
  • 1–3 years correct: 1 mark
  • All 4 required years correct: 2 marks
(Total 6 marks)

Data to plot: 1995 = 0%, 2000 = 20%, 2005 = 40%, 2010 = 60%.

If a histogram or line graph is drawn, marks will be lost for type of graph and scale.
If axes are transposed: can get all marks if labels are also swopped and bars are horizontal. If labels are not corresponding, marks will be lost for labels and scale; plotting can get credit if coordinates are correct for given labels.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why it would be expected that most of the individuals affected by haemophilia will be males.
subQuestions.memoText:
- Males have only one X-chromosome ✓ / XY
- If this chromosome carries the recessive allele the male will have haemophilia ✓
- as there is no other allele that could mask the effect of the recessive allele ✓
(3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why it would be expected that more stoneflies will have no wings in the areas without trees.

- Flying is dangerous ✓ in areas without trees
- However, stoneflies with no wings survived since they could not fly ✓
- Therefore, they reproduced ✓
- Passing the allele for no wings to the next generation ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how Lamarck would have explained the evolution of stoneflies without wings in the areas without trees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 5 of:
- All stoneflies had wings ✓
- Due to strong winds ✓ / since it was dangerous to fly in cleared areas
- They stopped using their wings ✓ / flying
- The wings became smaller ✓ / disappeared
- The acquired characteristic of no wings was passed on to the offspring ✓
- All offspring in the next generation had no wings ✓
(5 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of speciation through geographic isolation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 7 of:
- If a population of a single species becomes separated by a geographical barrier ✓ (sea, river, mountain, lake)
- then the population splits into two ✓
- There is no gene flow between the two populations ✓
- Each population may be exposed to different environmental conditions ✓ / the selection pressure may be different
- and therefore natural selection occurs independently ✓
- such that the individuals of the two populations become different ✓ genotypically and phenotypically ✓
- Even if these populations were to mix again ✓
- they will not be able to interbreed ✓
- because they are now different species ✓
(7 marks)
